Script: doc.symbolItems.add(doc.symbols.getByName("Data Storage")) in a document that holds the symbol; to use it in another document: app.open("<Illustrator 2026 install folder>/Presets/en_US/Symbols/Illuminate Flow Charts.ai"), place an instance there, item.duplicate(target.layers[0], ElementPlacement.PLACEATEND) (the symbol arrives in the target document), then close the library with SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES.

verified.note: Glossy blue circle with an aqua top and a square notch at the lower right, Q-like; the library's Process Flow Symbols sheet labels this shape Data Storage.

cards.name: Decision Diamond
cards.summary: Symbol 'Decision Diamond' from Illustrator's Illuminate Flow Charts symbol library: a glossy blue diamond (rhombus), wider than tall, with a lighter aqua top half and a thin pale inner outline, the flowchart shape for a decision. (Thumbnail: one instance placed from the library and fitted to 300 pt on white, applied by script; natural size about 34 x 22 pt; not a shipped preview.)
use_for: yes or no branches in a flowchart
avoid: text on its own: the shape holds no label; add one with the Type tool
long labels: the diamond has little text room
print-size use at natural size: it is only about 34 x 22 pt; scale it up (the gradients are vector and stay smooth)

cards.name: Delay
cards.summary: Symbol 'Delay' from Illustrator's Illuminate Flow Charts symbol library: a glossy blue D-shape, a rectangle with a fully rounded right end, lighter aqua on top and a darker band across the middle, the flowchart shape for a delay. (Thumbnail: one instance placed from the library and fitted to 300 pt on white, applied by script; natural size about 32 x 20 pt; not a shipped preview.)
use_for: wait or delay steps in a flowchart
avoid: text on its own: the shape holds no label; add one with the Type tool
a flat or print-friendly look: the glossy aqua-blue gradient is baked in; break the link and set a flat fill for one-colour work
print-size use at natural size: it is only about 32 x 20 pt; scale it up (the gradients are vector and stay smooth)
